production.note: US model years. First: BMW NA's release of 21 August 2017 is titled 'The All-New 2018 BMW M5' ('Available at certified BMW Centers in spring 2018'). BMW NA's 'The New 2021 BMW M5 Sedan' (bmw-us-2021-m5-release) prices the M5 Sedan at $103,500 alongside the M5 Competition Sedan. Last: Cars.com's 2023 M5 specification page lists the 'Sedan' trim with a '600.0-hp, 4.4-liter, 8 Cylinder Engine' (carscom-2023-m5-specs), and its 2024 page states 'The BMW M5 was not produced in 2024' (carscom-2024-m5); Machines With Souls' F90 buyer's guide says the car was 'Available from 2018' and 'still available from BMW through October of 2023' (mws-f90-m5-guide). No BMW NA page for the 2023 M5 was opened.

configuration.note: Cylinders 'V/8/4'; '4.4-liter V8 engine featuring M TwinPower Turbo technology' (bmw-us-2018-m5-release)

drivetrain.note: 'M xDrive' all-wheel drive with a selectable 2WD mode.

transmission.note: '8-speed M Steptronic transmission with Drivelogic' (torque-converter automatic), the only transmission.

powerHp.note: Quote: "Max output hp@rpm 600@5700 – 6600". Release (bmw-us-2018-m5-release): "600 hp and peak torque of 553 lb-ft". BMW NA's 2021 (facelift) release keeps the M5 at "600 hp @ 6,000 rpm" (bmw-us-2021-m5-release). The M5 Competition (617 hp) and M5 CS are separate variants.

weightLb.note: 2018 M5 Sedan, the only configuration (8-speed automatic, M xDrive). Quote: "US curb weight lb 4370". BMW NA's 2021 release gives 4,345 lb (bmw-us-2021-m5-release).

discrepancies.reason: Model year: BMW NA gives 4,370 lb for the 2018 M5 and 4,345 lb for the 2021 (facelift) M5.
discrepancies.resolution: Used 4,370 lb because the reference model year is 2018.
